title: What's Left When It Runs Out
logline: At a roadside food stall on a festival day, volunteers watch the queue grow longer than the food will stretch, and in the space of a few seconds, again and again, someone has to decide how to share what is left.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject. Object 2, acquired with wanting, may also be present at the moment the series first turns toward giving.

thread_in.thread: Inside that fast, unowned process there is still room to choose, and the next film finds it at a roadside free-food stall where, again and again, someone decides how to share what is left.

thread_out.thread: In that gap, goodness can be chosen: from a festival stall's free food to a roadside family that has fed passing strangers for years and hands Chathura a plate before he asks.

requirements: A roadside dansala or free food stall during a real religious festival, with organisers willing to allow filming
A festival day where demand plausibly outpaces supply, without the film creating or worsening any real shortage
Consent from volunteers and, where practical and respectful, from those being served

suggestions.name: A town along the Kataragama pilgrimage route during a festival period
suggestions.why: The Kataragama pilgrimage route has a long tradition of roadside dansala hospitality during festival seasons.
suggestions.season_notes: Timing would need to align with an actual festival or poya period with heavy pilgrim traffic.
suggestions.access_notes: Organisers' cooperation would be essential and filming must never slow down or interfere with real service.
suggestions.verify: A specific stall, organisers, and a festival date with genuinely constrained supply are unconfirmed.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.
